findings.finding: The plan specifies only the deterministic veto-side guard in pass3_decide but not the emit-side decision rule the verifier prompts must carry to set current_state_satisfies_plan_goal, unlike the a8e5 absence pair it explicitly mirrors, which ships a full co-located instruction block in the verifier prompt.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact criterion the verifier applies to answer current_state_satisfies_plan_goal='yes' at the FINDING level (the code's present state affirmatively realizes the plan's directed end state for THIS finding, distinguishing 'directed-and-done' from 'symbol absent because the work was skipped / the plan is wrong'), so the veto fires only on the completed-directed-work false-positive class.
evidence: Plan Approach: the veto drops the finding 'only when a new keyword-only execution_review flag is True AND the answer is a definite yes' — a per-finding drop keyed on a GOAL-level question

Problem statement scopes the target to findings that are 'the expected result of the plan's own directed work already having been done', but the mechanism (one goal-satisfaction binary) is coarser than that intent

A present-state 'does the goal hold now' check does not encode WHY a symbol is absent, so it cannot distinguish directed-removal-completed from work-skipped/plan-wrong — the two cases have identical present state
findings.finding: The veto's drop condition is a single binary 'current_state_satisfies_plan_goal' phrased as a GOAL-level present-state check ('does the code AS IT IS NOW already satisfy the plan's directed end state?'), but the plan needs it to fire ONLY on the narrow completed-directed-work false-positive class. A goal-satisfaction 'yes' cannot, by itself, separate (a) 'plan directed remove X and X is correctly gone' (drop) from (b) 'the plan references X because X should exist but the directed work was skipped/plan is wrong, so X is absent' (a true positive to keep) or (c) an unrelated genuine defect on a ticket whose overall goal is otherwise met. The plan states no answering criterion the verifier applies to distinguish these, so a definite 'yes' can veto legitimate execution-phase true positives.
findings.location: Approach paragraph ('set by the verifier via a present-state check: does the code AS IT IS NOW already satisfy the plan's directed end state?'); Acceptance Criteria bullet 1
scenarios: Execution review where a Pass-1 finding is a TRUE positive (directed work skipped, or a genuine defect introduced) but the verifier answers 'yes' because the plan's headline goal happens to be satisfied — a real defect is dropped and a broken ticket closes.
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe the sub-answer as a per-finding question ('is THIS finding the expected result of the plan's own directed work already being done, and does the present code realize that directed end state?') and add the affirmative answering protocol to the prompt docs so a bare goal-match cannot drop an unrelated true positive.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify why a NEW `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal` field is needed rather than extending/reusing the existing `asserted_capability_confirmed` sub-answer (decide.py:56, verify_models.py:66-88) — e.g. state the concrete semantic difference (standalone execution-phase veto vs. validity-axis refute) that makes reuse unworkable.
evidence: `asserted_capability_confirmed` is a member of GRADED_BINARY (decide.py:56) and is built onto EVERY verification model — including the plan-review model — via _build_binary iterating GRADED_BINARY (verify_models.py:102-104), so it already exists on the model the plan proposes to extend.

Its documented semantics (verify_models.py:66-75): 'for a finding asserting that a capability the plan/ticket claimed is NOT delivered by the code… no = the capability is in fact present and exercised, REFUTING the finding (lowers validity → a false non-delivery claim is dropped)' — the same shape as the plan's 'the plan directed remove/do X, X is done, so the discrepancy finding is a false positive'.
It is already na-default and cohort-restricted (verify_models.py:66-88), the SAME two properties the plan re-specifies for its new field.
The plan cites the asserted_capability_confirmed cohort restriction only as a pattern to MIRROR, never as a field to potentially EXTEND to the plan-review execution phase.
findings.finding: The plan mints a NEW binary sub-answer `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal` whose purpose — refute a plan-vs-code discrepancy finding when the code already satisfies the plan's directed end state, dropping the false positive — closely overlaps the ALREADY-EXISTING `asserted_capability_confirmed` sub-answer, which the plan-review model already carries and which is documented to refute exactly such a 'directed work already delivered, so the gap finding is false' claim; the plan does not analyze whether extending/reusing that field is viable before adding a new one.
findings.location: Approach ('A new plan-review-only binary sub-answer current_state_satisfies_plan_goal') and Scope (verify_models.py bullet)
scenarios: An implementer adds a second near-identical refute sub-answer, leaving two overlapping fields whose scopes (validity-axis vs. veto; code-review vs. plan-review execution) a future reader must disentangle.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive rationale for the new binary: state why the completed-directed-work false positive cannot be handled by phase-gating an existing mechanism (note a8e5 is opposite-polarity — it refutes a claimed absence, whereas here the absence is genuine), so the reader can judge the chosen approach is the best available.
evidence: decide.py:575 — the a8e5 veto fires on `claims_absence == 'yes' AND absence_confirmed_in_context == 'no'` (a REFUTED absence), the OPPOSITE of the plan's case where the absence is genuine/expected

orchestrator.pass3_over_findings already threads execution_review and raises block_threshold to 0.80 under execution (orchestrator.py:675) — an existing execution-phase lever the plan does not weigh against a new veto
The Approach asserts the mechanism 'mirrors' a8e5 and does a 'present-state check' but states no positive reason a new binary is required rather than phase-gating an existing one
findings.finding: The plan adds a NEW (third) Pass-2 veto binary but provides no POSITIVE rationale for why the chosen approach beats extending an existing mechanism. It justifies the binary only by analogy ('mirroring the existing a8e5 absence-refuted veto'), yet a8e5 is opposite-polarity — it drops when a claimed absence is REFUTED (the thing actually exists), whereas here the absence is REAL (X was correctly removed), so a8e5 would not fire and the 'mirror' framing does not carry the design justification. Nor does the plan say why a phase-gated reuse of the existing execution_review machinery (which already floors the block threshold at 0.80 in orchestrator.pass3_over_findings) or the divergent_implementation grade cannot address the same false-positive class. G6 requires a positive fit rationale; its absence leaves the reader unable to judge the new binary is the best-available approach rather than an added veto surface.
findings.location: Approach section ('Add a single-answer Pass-2 VETO, mirroring the existing a8e5 absence-refuted veto')
scenarios: A reviewer/implementer asks why a third veto binary was added instead of reusing existing execution-phase machinery, and the plan gives no rationale to defend the choice — risking either an unjustified new veto surface or a needless rebuild.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach, replace the bare 'mirroring a8e5' framing with a one-paragraph rationale: the false positive is a REAL, expected absence (directed removal completed), which a8e5's refuted-absence veto and the divergent_implementation grade do not target, and the existing 0.80 execution floor cannot drop; hence a distinct definite-yes veto is required.

findings.finding: The veto trusts `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal="yes"` as a present-state fact, but the plan-review Pass-2 verifier only runs code-grounded (agentic, tool-equipped to inspect the current code) for findings citing a CODEBASE_GROUNDED criterion (E4/G1G2/A1/G6); a finding outside that cohort is verified single-turn without tools, so its `yes` is not a real present-state check yet would still fire the drop.
findings.location: Approach / Scope (verify_models.py new na-default binary; decide.py veto branch); cf. workflow_ops.py:272-289 plan_review_grounding and verify_models.py:66-88 asserted_capability_confirmed
findings.suggested_fix: Document in the field description (and the two verifier prompts) that `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal` stays `na` unless the finding is in the code-grounded cohort where the agentic verifier can actually inspect present code state, mirroring the asserted_capability_confirmed cohort restriction; add an AC/test that a non-grounded single-turn verification does not produce a definite `yes`.

findings.finding: The veto fires on a definite `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal="yes"`, which asserts the code AS IT IS NOW satisfies the plan's directed end state — a present-state CODE check — but the plan does not specify how the non-tool-using single-turn verifier is to perform that check, nor a fallback (e.g. answer `na`) when it has no code access.
findings.location: Scope bullet: plan_review_verifier.md / plan_review_verifier_agentic.md ('document the sub-answer'); Approach ('set by the verifier via a present-state check')
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope/prompt-doc bullet, add the answer-setting rule: the agentic verifier sets "yes" only after confirming via read_file/search_files that current code already satisfies the plan's directed end state; the single-turn verifier defaults to "na" (never a definite "yes") since it has no code access.
